claim: When every bird sees every other and only alignment is on, the total velocity of the flock never changes.
derivation: World 16 × 16 with R = 12: the longest short-way distance on this torus is √(8² + 8²) ≈ 11.31 < 12, so every bird always sees the other three (E1, E2).
With only alignment on, Σ A_i = w_a Σ (ū_i − v_i), and ū_i = (V − v_i)/3 with V = Σ v_j, so Σ ū_i = (4V − V)/3 = V and the sum is zero (E3).
v′_i = (1 − w_a Δt) v_i + w_a Δt ū_i with w_a Δt = 0.025 is a convex combination of current velocities, so every velocity stays in the triangle (2, 0), (0, 2), (2, 2).
Speeds therefore stay within [√2, 2√2] ⊂ [0.45, 3.6] and |a| ≤ 1.5 · 2√2 ≈ 4.24 < 50, so neither clamp acts (E8, E9).
The total velocity stays (5, 5) at every one of 120 steps; only floating-point rounding can move it.
